title: ITC Maurya Hosts Vladimir Putin in Grand Presidential Suite, Delhi
text:
From Clinton To Putin: This Iconic Delhi Hotel Continues Its Legacy Of Hosting Global Heads Of State
Curated By :
Edited By:
Last Updated:
Russian President Vladimir Putin’s stay at Delhi’s ITC Maurya highlights the hotel’s legacy of hosting world leaders and global icons.
1/7
When Russian President Vladimir Putin will land in New Delhi today, he will join the long list of world leaders and celebrities who have chosen the ITC Maurya as their residence during official trips to India. Known for its opulence, security, and unmatched hospitality, the hotel has become the preferred address for visiting heads of state.
2/7
Putin will be accommodated in the hotel’s Grand Presidential Suite, famously called Chanakya. This mansion-like suite is designed to meet the highest standards of luxury and security.
ADVERTISEMENT
3/7
The suite has been tailored to host dignitaries with utmost discretion and comfort, making it a symbol of ITC Maurya’s reputation as India’s “hotel of presidents.” Putin’s stay adds another chapter to the hotel’s storied history of welcoming global icons.
4/7
Over the years, ITC Maurya has hosted several US Presidents, including George W. Bush, Bill Clinton, Barack Obama, Jimmy Carter, and Donald Trump. UK Prime Minister Tony Blair has also stayed here previously.
ADVERTISEMENT
5/7
The Dalai Lama, sports icons like Roger Federer, Tiger Woods, Sachin Tendulkar, and M.S. Dhoni, and celebrities including Mick Jagger, Arnold Schwarzenegger, and painter M.F. Husain, have also stayed at the ITC Maurya.
6/7
The hotel’s legendary restaurant, Bukhara, is adorned with photographs of its distinguished diners. From Tony Blair and Bill Clinton to cricketing legends and global celebrities, the walls tell the story of ITC Maurya’s unparalleled guest list. Putin’s visit further cements the restaurant’s reputation as a dining destination for the world’s elite.
